Package com.nexuslink.ui.controls

Class ConnectionChip

java.lang.Object
javafx.scene.Node
javafx.scene.Parent
javafx.scene.layout.Region
javafx.scene.layout.Pane
javafx.scene.layout.StackPane
com.nexuslink.ui.controls.ConnectionChip
All Implemented Interfaces:
javafx.css.Styleable, javafx.event.EventTarget
public final class ConnectionChip extends javafx.scene.layout.StackPane
A connection string shown the way a connection string should be: as a short chip naming what you are connected to, which turns into a full editable field only when you actually want to edit it.

Two problems with a permanently expanded text box. It eats the toolbar — a Mongo URI with a replica set and options is longer than the rest of the controls put together, so everything else gets squeezed. And it puts any embedded password on display: mongodb://app:s3cret@… is a password on every screenshot and screen share. The chip shows db.internal:27017/orders (or the saved connection's name), keeps the real value intact underneath, and reveals it only on demand.

Double-click, Enter, or the edit button opens the editor; Enter commits, Escape cancels back to the value it had. The full string is never shown while collapsed — the tooltip and the copy action are redacted too — so a reveal is always a deliberate act.
